title: 공공 예절: 줄을 서고, 조용히 해요
objective: By the end, you can use 10 public-manners words, such as 줄, 차례, 조용히 and 떠들다, in short sentences. You can also tell whether something people do in public is polite or not.
summary: Ten everyday words for good manners in public places in Korea, such as standing in line, keeping quiet, and giving up your seat.

task.title: Use the words correctly
task.line: Read each sentence and choose, write, or judge using the words you learned on page 1.

words.exampleMeaning: I want to learn Korean table manners.

words.meaning: line, queue (줄을 서다 = to stand in line)
words.example: 버스를 타려고 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요.
words.exampleMeaning: People are standing in line to get on the bus.
Please call me when it's my turn.
The baby is sleeping, so please be quiet.

words.example: 옆집이 너무 시끄러워서 잠을 못 잤어요.
words.exampleMeaning: The house next door was so noisy that I couldn't sleep.

words.meaning: to talk loudly, to make noise by chatting
words.exampleMeaning: You must not talk loudly in the library.

words.meaning: sound; volume (of a phone, TV, etc.)
words.exampleMeaning: Please turn down your phone's volume a little.

words.meaning: to give up (a seat, a place) for someone else
words.exampleMeaning: I gave my seat to an elderly woman on the subway.

words.meaning: to follow, to keep (a rule, an order)
words.exampleMeaning: Please wait your turn. (lit. Please keep the order.)
Please throw your trash in the trash can.

exercises: Fill in the blank with one word from the list: 병원 대기실에서는 ____ 기다려 주세요.
Fill in the blank with one word from the list: 주말이라서 화장실 앞에 ____이 길어요.
Choose the right word: ① 어른 앞에서는 (예절 / 차례)을 잘 지켜야 해요. ② 버스에서 임산부에게 자리를 (양보했어요 / 떠들었어요). ③ 공연 중에는 휴대폰 (소리 / 쓰레기)를 꺼 주세요. ④ 지금 누구 (차례 / 줄)예요?
Is this good manners? Write O (yes) or X (no): ① 도서관에서 친구와 크게 떠들어요. ② 엘리베이터 앞에서 줄을 서서 기다려요. ③ 공원 벤치에 쓰레기를 두고 가요. ④ 식당에서 순서를 잘 지켜요.
Fill in the blank with the past tense of a word from the list: 영화관에서 뒷사람들이 너무 ____. 그래서 "조용히 해 주세요."라고 말했어요.
answers: ① 예절 ② 양보했어요 ③ 소리 ④ 차례
① X ② O ③ X ④ O
